retry_guidance_rules.subject: C
messages: Retry target for C PE: build a small lab task around reading two or more values and printing a derived result, comparison result, or short formatted summary. Avoid parity-only, even/odd, or single-threshold pass/fail drills unless the chunks explicitly center that exact behavior.

retry_guidance_rules.subject: C
messages: Retry target for C PE: prefer a comparison task grounded in relational operators, such as LESS/EQUAL/GREATER for two integers or the larger of a small set of integers. Do not reuse the generic PASS/FAIL threshold pattern.

retry_guidance_rules.subject: C
messages: Retry target for C PE: use arithmetic in a learner-facing task with at least one meaningful behavior rule, derived value, or small decision. Avoid quotient/remainder exactness wrappers and direct lecture-formula replays.

retry_guidance_rules.subject: JAVA_OOP
messages: Retry target for Java OOP PE on abstract classes: avoid thin template tasks where an abstract base only forces one trivial label/message override. Prefer a learner-facing task where the abstract parent keeps shared state or a shared concrete helper, and each subclass must contribute one meaningful behavior rule that changes the final result in a visible way. Keep the task concept-near and grounded in inherited behavior, validation, status evaluation, summary building, or another chunk-supported purpose. Do not drift into invented business pricing/payment stories, and do not use anonymous-class demos unless the chunks clearly support them.

retry_guidance_rules.subject: JAVA_OOP
messages: Retry target for Java OOP PE: avoid invented fee/payment/balance/shipping business stories, avoid one-line arithmetic override differences, and avoid toString-only tasks where subclasses merely reformat the same fields. Prefer parent-reference dispatch with inherited state plus a clearer behavior difference, such as different computed summaries, status evaluation, or another chunk-grounded behavior beyond simple string rearrangement. If the chunks are too thin, generate fewer but cleaner items.

Retry target for Java OOP PE on polymorphism: produce a distinct learner-facing scenario where inherited state and overridden behavior both matter. Prefer one shared parent helper or summary method plus a subclass-specific rule that changes the final result in a visible way.
Do not copy lecture-demo nouns, method names, or output patterns from the cited chunks even if they are grounded. Ground the behavior, not the exact example family.

retry_guidance_rules.subject: DSA_JAVA
messages: Retry target for DSA Java PE on queue/array topics: do not regenerate the full lecture API clone with enqueue/front/dequeue/isEmpty under lightly renamed commands. That is too close to the cited queue example.

Prefer one narrower learner-facing behavior grounded in the chunks, such as circular reuse after removals, counting failed insertions, reporting final queue state, validating wrap-around behavior, or tracking size/empty transitions after a command sequence.

If fixed capacity is required, say explicitly that this assessment uses a non-growing circular array queue and that full arrivals are rejected. Do not silently contradict grow() from the source chunks.
Avoid service-desk wrappers when they only rename the queue operations. The new task must add a clearer behavior goal beyond basic API simulation.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: C
messages: For C PE, keep the task small and learner-facing, but do not collapse it into parity-only, pass/fail-only, or a direct formula replay unless the cited chunks explicitly center that exact behavior.
For C PE, prefer chunk-supported derived results, comparisons, small classifications, or short formatted summaries over generic threshold wrappers.
Do not invent file I/O, advanced libraries, structs, pointers, or other APIs unless the cited chunks explicitly support them.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: C
messages: For C PE on variables or input/output, do not generate a pure read-and-echo exercise that only scans values and prints them back with labels.
Prefer a small learner-facing task where variables are assigned, reused, compared, or combined into one short derived result or short labeled summary that still stays in beginner C scope.
If the source mainly supports variable declaration and basic memory operations, avoid overfitting to a long real-world story unless the cited chunks clearly provide that scenario.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: C
messages: For C PE on arithmetic operators, stay close to the grounded arithmetic behavior and avoid adding an extra multi-branch classification layer unless relational logic is clearly supported by the cited chunks.
Do not create learner-facing outputs like GREATER/EQUAL/SMALLER or similar status labels unless the task also has grounded comparison support and test coverage for every required branch.
Prefer small numeric-result tasks, short comparisons already evidenced by the source, or one simple derived behavior rather than stacking multiple invented requirements.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: JAVA_OOP
messages: For Java OOP PE on polymorphism, avoid invented business pricing/payment/shipping stories when the chunks mainly support simpler inherited behavior or code-dispatch patterns.
Do not generate thin subclass tasks where each subclass only changes a fixed label, message, formatting string, or one-line arithmetic return.
Prefer inherited state plus one meaningful overridden behavior that changes the final result in a visible, chunk-grounded way.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: JAVA_OOP
messages: For Java OOP PE on abstract classes, do not generate a thin template where the abstract parent only forces one cosmetic label/message override.
Prefer an abstract parent with shared state or shared helper behavior, and make each subclass contribute one visible chunk-grounded rule.
Do not drift into anonymous-class or one-off subclass demos unless the cited chunks clearly support that subtopic.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: DSA_JAVA
messages: For DSA Java PE on priority queues, do not invent a new sorting rule, tie-break rule, min-vs-max convention, or output ordering contract unless the cited chunks clearly support it.

Do not silently switch the source behavior from grow-on-full to fixed-capacity rejection unless the description explicitly states that the assessment intentionally uses a non-growing variant and the cited chunks support that simplification.

Prefer a task centered on chunk-supported priority-queue behavior such as dequeue/front semantics, priority-based removal, or a small array-backed implementation behavior that stays close to the cited operations and constraints.

generation_guidance_rules.subject: DSA_JAVA
messages: For DSA Java PE on queue/array topics, do not regenerate a broad lecture API clone unless the task adds a clearly stated learner-facing behavior goal beyond simple enqueue/dequeue simulation.
Avoid pulling deque behavior, round-robin scheduling, or unrelated queue applications into the task unless those concepts are truly part of the selected topic support.

issue_messages.duplicate_options: FE options contain duplicates or near-duplicates.
issue_messages.forbidden_meta_option: FE uses a forbidden meta option pattern such as 'All of the above' or 'None of the above'.
issue_messages.missing_question_mark: FE stem should read as a clear question.

issue_messages.near_copy_lecture_demo: PE shape is too close to a lecture-example pattern and only renames the original demo with cosmetic changes.
issue_messages.message_only_subclass: PE polymorphism shape is too weak because subclasses differ mainly by fixed labels or message strings.
issue_messages.to_string_only_weak_task: PE polymorphism shape is still too weak because the learner mainly overrides one formatting/display method and does not implement richer object behavior.
issue_messages.invented_ordering_behavior: PE introduces a new ordering or sorting rule that is not supported by the cited chunks, so the grounding is too weak.
issue_messages.trivial_polymorphism_arithmetic: PE polymorphism shape is too template-like: abstract base plus two subclasses with one-line arithmetic overrides is not yet a strong learner-facing assessment task.
issue_messages.formula_only_demo: PE shape is still a formula-demo exercise that mirrors lecture syntax too directly and lacks enough learner-facing assessment value.
issue_messages.parity_drill: PE shape is only an even/odd parity drill, which is too weak and too generic for the current source-backed PE quality target.
issue_messages.exact_not_exact_drill: PE shape is only an exact/not-exact remainder wrapper around a lecture-style arithmetic example and does not add enough assessment value.
issue_messages.uncovered_comparison_branch: PE introduces comparison-classification output such as GREATER/EQUAL/SMALLER but the tests do not cover all required branches.
issue_messages.pass_fail_threshold_copy: PE shape is too close to a generic PASS/FAIL threshold exemplar and is not clearly grounded in the selected source topic.
issue_messages.binary_threshold_status_template: PE shape is still too generic: a binary threshold-based status wrapper like COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE or YES/NO does not create enough OOP-specific assessment value for this grounded PE flow.
issue_messages.queue_api_clone: PE queue/array shape is too close to the cited lecture queue API and only wraps enqueue/front/dequeue/isEmpty with lightly renamed commands such as ARRIVE/NEXT/SERVE.
issue_messages.queue_capacity_drift: PE queue/array shape changes the source behavior from grow-on-full to fixed-capacity rejection without clearly stating that the assessment intentionally uses a non-growing circular queue variant.
issue_messages.thin_abstract_template: PE abstract-class shape is too weak: the abstract parent and subclasses only support a thin label/message template instead of a meaningful inherited behavior task.
issue_messages.abstract_formatting_clone: PE abstract-class shape is still too template-like because the learner mainly overrides one formatting or summary method with cosmetic subclass differences.
issue_messages.anonymous_or_one_off_subclass: PE abstract-class shape drifts into an anonymous or one-off subclass demo that is too code-shape-driven and not a strong learner-facing assessment item.
issue_messages.abstract_single_subclass_rule_wrapper: PE abstract-class shape is still too thin: one abstract parent plus one concrete subclass wrapping a simple conditional rule does not create enough abstract-class-specific assessment value.
